name: coachmark
title: Coachmark
description: One step of a tour, pointing at the control it explains.
use: A short explanation tied to one place on the page: what a new control does, or one step of a tour through a screen. A beacon marks the place and opens it, or a script opens the steps of a tour in turn. Keep it to a title, a sentence and a way on; the reader should be able to leave a tour at any step.

instead.when: It is a few words that name a control, with nothing in it to act on
The content belongs to a button and is opened for its own sake, such as a share link or a short form
The reader must answer before going on
It says where the reader is in a sequence of pages or a form

keyboard.action: On the beacon: open or close its coachmark. An action inside with autofocus takes focus as it opens
Move between the actions in the coachmark, and from it back to the page after the beacon
Close a coachmark opened with popover="auto" and return focus to the beacon. A tour's steps are popover="manual", so the tour's script closes them on Escape

platform.feature: The popover attribute with popovertarget on a beacon, or showPopover({ source }) from a tour's script
platform.fallback: Supported in all current browsers. Where the source option of showPopover() is missing, a tour's step opens without an anchor, where the browser places a popover

platform.feature: CSS anchor positioning (position-area, position-try-fallbacks and anchor() with anchor-name and anchor-scope)
platform.fallback: The coachmark still opens and closes; it appears centered in the viewport, where the browser places any popover, and has no arrow
The coachmark appears and leaves at once, without the fade and the short slide

classes.name: coachmark
classes.description: The card of ink, on an element with the popover attribute and role="dialog", labelled by its title; without the popover attribute it is never shown. It opens centered under the element that opened it, flips above when there is no room, and is 18rem wide. Its arrow points at the element right before it in the markup, so put it right after its beacon or the control it explains

classes.name: coachmark-top
classes.description: Prefers the space above, for a control near the foot of the screen or a beacon on a control's top corner

classes.name: coachmark-count
classes.description: A short line over the title in a quieter ink: where the step stands in the tour (2 of 4), or a word such as New

classes.name: coachmark-title
classes.description: The heading of the step, which labels the coachmark

classes.name: coachmark-text
classes.description: One or two sentences that say what the control does

classes.name: coachmark-actions
classes.description: A row of small buttons along the foot, 12px from the card's edges: the first of several stands at the start (Skip), the others at the end (Back, Next). A default button reads as the action on ink, and a quiet one takes the card's ink

classes.name: coachmark-beacon
classes.description: A 10px dot of ink that marks where a step is and opens it with popovertarget. It sends out a ring now and then, which rests as a halo while it is under the pointer, has focus or its coachmark is open, and under reduced motion. Its target is 24px, and 44px on a touch screen. The page places it, usually on the top corner of the control it marks

states.name: open
states.description: Shown in the top layer, faded in and slid 4px toward the element that opened it

states.name: found
states.description: Its coachmark, right after it, is open: the ring rests as a halo

properties.name: --coachmark-width
properties.description: The card's width, never wider than the viewport less a rem

properties.name: --coachmark-inset
properties.description: Space between the actions and the card's edges; the text has 4px more. The card's corner is a small button's corner plus this inset

properties.name: --coachmark-arrow
properties.description: How far the arrow's point stands out from the card

properties.name: --anchored-gap
properties.description: Space between the card and the element that opened it; the arrow's point stands 6px from that element
